EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
2027 ROG 14RKB Continues To Have One of the Weirdest Bathrooms – Built for Tough Glamping Scenarios
26 photos
Photo: Encore RV
“ It’s not stupid if it works ” seems to be one of the phrases that comes to mind upon exploring the 2027 ROG 14RKB from Encore RV. It’s possible you have an idea of what this camper has in store based on previous model years, but if you’re not aware of what the 14RKB class brings to the table, prepare to be surprised, to say the least.
Ladies and gents, most campers on the market these days follow some very similar guidelines and styling, so when something that breaks the mold hits the scene , you can bet that the world is all eyes and ears. That’s precisely what happened when the ROG 14RKB was first introduced as a 2024 model.
Since then, outdoor lover after outdoor lover has had something to say about this one, sometimes, positive, sometimes, negative, and it all really makes sense.
Photo: Encore RV The 14RKB has always stood apart from other campers in its class with a rather unique interior for a square drop, with the highlight being the enclosed and complete wet bath inside, accessible via the rear. This means that you can shower and “meditate” in the morning without having to worry about prying eyes or creepy crawlers riding up your legs.
However, there is one massive catch here, and it’s the fact that showers are to be carried out sitting down. Simply put, there isn’t enough space to stand inside one of these bathrooms, making for some questionable acrobatics in order to clean your nooks and crannies.
It’s an odd position, to say the least, but does have one particular benefit that some people overlook: showering with a view. Since the bathroom is located at the rear of the unit, all you have to do is back this thing up to a mountain ledge looking east, and once the sun starts to rise over the horizon, wake up and take a shower while leaving the rear door open and enjoy . The same is true for other bathroom-oriented activities.
Photo: Encore RV One thing that I can say about the 14RKB is that is does truly invite its owners to take in the outside world, and aside from doing your thing with the bathroom door wide open, the kitchen also invites us to spend time in nature.
It does so by being mounted into the shell of the 14RKB. The main block is located on a slide-out that tucks into the rear right hand corner of the camper. This slide-out allows us to access a sink with faucet, cooktop, and ample storage for gas, water, and utensils, while a side-mounted griddle can also be called upon, located on the camping side of the unit.
The fridge, or should I say, fridges, are hidden behind a hatch over the griddle. Two are in place and completed the galley features. All this sits underneath a batwing awning, so we don’t sizzle away in the sun like our burger patties.
Photo: Encore RV While some reviews for the 14RKB mention that space is limited, I found the interior to be quite roomy, capable of handling a queen-sized modular mattress that can double as a seating arrangement for at least three people. I’m thinking folks were most likely referring to the size of the bathroom.
The interior is also equipped with ample storage, some of the largest bays I’ve seen in a camper of this style, and the possibility to add a TV. A sound system is in place, along with control panel too, window blinds, and even heating or AC, depending on what seasons of the year you want to tackle.
The 14RKB is also decently strong in the off-grid features department, with the manufacturer’s spec sheet showcasing battery arrays with as much as 400 Ah, solar panels of up to 400 W, and 3,000 W inverter, DC-DC charger, and a couple others. Two trim levels are available to choose from and more options do exist , including beefing up the suspension to an axle-less one and adding an articulating hitch.
To sum it all up, this one can take us off the beaten path, but does have some limits, one of which is a GVWR of 4,400 lbs (1,996 kg), with a dry weight, in its lightest configuration, of 2,283 lbs (1,035 kg).
Photo: Encore RV This leaves us with around 2,100 lbs of cargo-carrying capacity and the roof rack is the perfect place to add heavier items that can be exposed to the elements. I’s also a great place to add an RTT (roof-top tent), expanding this campers accommodation to an entire family of at least four guests, depending on the size of your tent.
I’m curious to hear your thoughts on what this RV brings to the table and how. Be sure to check out the little clip below for a better POV on things.
Last but not least, we have the price for one of these babies, which, according to Encore RV , is set with an MSRP of $36,321 (€33,120) for a baseline 2027 ROG 14RKB. Depending on trim levels and extras, a 2027 version can run close to $50K, with most dealers hovering around $45K.
